hints: Differentiate the displacement function $s(t) = 0.004(75t^2 - t^3)$ to find the velocity function $v(t)$.
Find when the cyclist comes to rest at B by setting $v(t) = 0$ for $t > 0$, giving $t = 50\text{ s}$.
Substitute $t = 50$ into $s(t)$ to show that the distance $AB$ is $250\text{ m}$.
walkthrough:
State the relationship between velocity and displacement: velocity is the time derivative of displacement:
$$v(t) = \frac{ds}{dt}$$

Determine the time when the cyclist reaches point $B$, where the cyclist comes to rest ($v = 0$):
$$0.012t(50 - t) = 0$$
Since $t = 0$ corresponds to starting at $A$, the non-zero solution gives the arrival at $B$:
$$t = 50\text{ s}$$

Substitute $t = 50$ into the displacement formula $s(t)$:
$$s(50) = 0.004(75(50^2) - 50^3)$$
Compute each power of $50$:
$$50^2 = 2500$$
$$75(2500) = 187500$$
$$50^3 = 125000$$
Subtract:
$$187500 - 125000 = 62500$$
Multiply by $0.004$:
$$s(50) = 0.004 \times 62500 = 250\text{ m}$$
Thus the distance $AB$ is $250\text{ m}$ as required.

hints: Maximum velocity occurs when acceleration $\frac{dv}{dt} = 0$ (or by using the symmetry of the parabola between $t = 0$ and $t = 50$).
Differentiate $v(t) = 0.6t - 0.012t^2$ to find $a(t) = 0.6 - 0.024t$, and solve for $t = 25\text{ s}$.
Substitute $t = 25\text{ s}$ into the velocity function to find $v_{\text{max}}$.
walkthrough:
Find the time of maximum velocity by differentiating $v(t)$ to obtain the acceleration function and setting it to zero:
$$a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}(0.6t - 0.012t^2) = 0.6 - 0.024t$$

Set $a(t) = 0$:
$$0.6 - 0.024t = 0$$
$$0.024t = 0.6$$
Divide both sides by $0.024$:
$$t = \frac{0.6}{0.024} = 25\text{ s}$$
(Note that $\frac{d^2v}{dt^2} = -0.024 < 0$, verifying a maximum turning point).

Substitute $t = 25$ into the velocity function:
$$v_{\text{max}} = 0.6(25) - 0.012(25^2)$$
Compute each term:
$$0.6(25) = 15$$
$$0.012(625) = 7.5$$
Subtract:
$$v_{\text{max}} = 15 - 7.5 = 7.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Thus the maximum velocity of the cyclist is $7.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
